title: The Big Misconception About Electricity
subject: Physics
beats: Thought experiment: light-second-long wires, bulb 1 m from the switch; how long until it lights?
Offers 5 options and asks you to commit in the comments before the reveal
States the idealizations: no resistance, bulb lights instantly
In AC the electrons only wiggle, so how does energy reach your home?
His old teaching analogy: electrons as a chain in a tube, pushed by the plant
The analogy is wrong: transformers break the wire; why doesn't returning current carry energy back?
Names the lies: electrons hold energy, a continuous loop, energy dissipated by electrons
Maxwell: light is oscillating electric and magnetic fields
Poynting traces energy flow locally, starting from sunlight
Poynting vector S = E x B over mu naught
Cross product explained with the right-hand rule
For light, energy flows the way light travels: makes sense
The kicker: it works anywhere E and B coincide
Simple battery-and-bulb circuit: field extends at light speed, surface charges build
Electron drift is only about 0.1 mm per second
Applies the right-hand rule around the battery, along the wires, at the bulb
Experts: people think they're buying electrons; energy moves through the space around wires
Electrons go both ways, energy only one way: fields carry it
AC: E and B flip together, so energy still flows source to bulb
Not academic: the 1858 transatlantic cable failed; Kelvin's water-tube view vs Heaviside's fields
Iron sheath raised capacitance; why power lines hang high above damp ground
Answer: about 1/c seconds; the field crosses the 1 m gap in nanoseconds
The bulb gets only a fraction of voltage at first; experts disagreed on details
Jokes about building desert power lines if called out
We use this daily and almost nobody knows; think of it at every light switch
